comment: Cases where the pyte pseudo-oracle genuinely diverges from xterm.js. These are pyte limitations/behaviors, verified by hand against the corpus bytes; xterm.js matches DEC/xterm documented behavior in each. The compare step exits 0 when the only failures are listed here, and exits 1 if a listed case starts passing (stale entry). This file applies to xterm-vs-PYTE runs; a real iTerm2 fixture run should start with an empty list.

divergences.reason: pyte has no alternate screen buffer: DECSET 1049 is recorded in Screen.mode but drawing continues on the primary buffer, so main-screen text stays visible
pyte has no alternate screen buffer: content drawn 'in the alt screen' bleeds onto the primary buffer and survives DECRST 1049
pyte does not implement ANSI save/restore cursor (SCOSC/SCORC, CSI s / CSI u); xterm.js restores the saved position
pyte does not home the cursor when DECSTBM (CSI r) is set/reset; xterm.js moves to (1,1) per DEC STD-070
pyte does not home the cursor when DECSTBM (CSI r) is set/reset; xterm.js moves to (1,1) per DEC STD-070
pyte does not implement SGR 2 (dim/faint); the pyte runner hard-reports dim=false
pyte draws a wide char whose second column would overflow into the last column anyway; xterm.js (like iTerm2) wraps the whole glyph to the next row
